report.source_text: Emergency whole-spine contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a huge intramedullary thoracic lesion extending from T5 to T8 that was hyperintense in T2-weighted images (Figure 1a), with scattered enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1b). Additionally, there was a round intradural extramedullary mass lesion at the L1 and L2 levels causing a compression effect on the conus medullaris that was isointense in T2-wighted images (Figure 1c), with homogenous enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1d).

report.source_text: On physical examination at the current presentation, the patient’s muscle strength in her lower extremities was as follows: right: 3/5 and left: 1/5 (proximal/distal, respectively). There was a sensory level in the thoracic region (T6), and spastic hyperreflexia was present in the lower extremities (American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) impairment scale C). Urinary sphincter function was intact, but the patient complained of incomplete evacuation of the bladder. A urodynamic study revealed a spastic bladder. Bilateral Babinski reflexes were upward.

report.source_text: Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion revealed small round cells with moderate pleomorphism, nuclear atypia, and some true rosette formations in a pauci-vascular background (Figure 3a). Immunohistochemical staining of the tumor showed diffuse, strong immunoreactivity for cluster of differentiation (CD)99, and a high proliferative index (Ki-67: 85%–90%), with negative staining for leukocyte common antigen (LCA) (Figure 3b–d).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old woman with prior left clavicular Ewing sarcoma treated and in remission presented with progressive paraparesis and sensory deficits at T6 level. MRI spine revealed a large intramedullary thoracic lesion T5-T8 and an intradural extramedullary mass at L1-L2 compressing the conus medullaris. Physical exam confirmed paraparesis, spastic hyperreflexia, and a spastic bladder. Histopathology of the thoracic lesion showed small round cells with CD99 positivity and high proliferation index, consistent with Ewing sarcoma. Neurological status worsened at 10 months follow-up. Molecular testing for EWSR1 rearrangement was ordered but no result was documented.

Physical exam showed progressive paraparesis with muscle strength right 3/5, left 1/5, sensory level at T6, spastic hyperreflexia, and spastic bladder on urodynamic study
Histopathology demonstrated small round cells with CD99 positivity and high Ki-67 proliferation consistent with Ewing sarcoma
At 10-month follow-up, patient's neurological function worsened to ASIA impairment scale B with spasticity and urofecal retention
